newsitem.title: INDIA: Thousands evacuated in India as cyclone nears.
newsitem.headline: Thousands evacuated in India as cyclone nears.

text.p: Authorities evacuated more than 300,000 coastal villagers to safety in India's southeastern state of Andhra Pradesh where a powerful cyclone was expected to cross around noon on Thursday, officials said.

"The cyclone is meandering about 90 km (56 miles) off the coast and could now probably hit land around noon (0630 GMT)," J.V.M Naidu, director of the cyclone warning centre at Visakhapatnam port, told Reuters.

Late on Wednesday, meteorological officials said the cyclone was expected to cross land between Ongole town and Kakinada port at about 2.00 a.m. on Thursday (2030 GMT Wednesday). An earlier forecast said it would reach land around noon on Wednesday.
Officials said more than 300,000 people from 600 coastal villages were moved to 700 relief camps in the five districts of East and West Godavari, Krishna, Prakasam and Guntur.
The storm, the second in a month in the state, claimed its first two victims on Wednesday.
One person was killed after a house collapsed and the other crushed under an uprooted tree as strong winds swept the coast ahead of the storm, they said.

Officials said the latest cyclone could inflict more damage to property and crops than last month's cyclone which left left more than 2,000 people dead or missing at sea and caused 50 billion rupees ($1.4 billion) in crop and property damage.
"The second sowing season has just begun. A storm is the worst thing that can happen now," said one official.

Port officials in Kakinada said they had moved nine ships from the harbour to avoid expected rough seas. Rail and road services were suspended and power switched off in areas likely to be affected by the cyclone.
The storm, with gale force winds of up to 180 kph (113 miles per hour), was steadily moving northwesterly across the Bay of Bengal toward the coast.
Naidu said the storm's slowing pace could indicate that it was intensifying.

The storm is expected to whip up winds of 150-180 kph (94-113 miles per hour) and tidal waves two to three metres high (six to nine feet) which are expected to flood low-lying areas up to 10 km (six miles) inland, officials said.
Chitra Ramachandran, Krishna district administrator, said all women and children have been evacuated from coastal areas.
Ramachandran said a 90 km (55 mile)-long and 15-km (nine mile) wide strip of the coast was declared a "no-man's zone" as the storm threatened to rip through villages lying in its path.
Most of last month's storm damage was confined to two districts of East and West Godavari. The two deaths from the latest storm were reported from East Godavari.
In November 1977, a cyclone killed more than 10,000 people in the Diviseema region near Machilipatnam in the same Andhra Pradesh state.
